export const DATA_SOURCES_HTML = `

Data sources

  • Winds (MCMC FV3 Mars GCM, beta release 1): hourly lowest-level winds, temperature and surface pressure of the NASA Ames Mars Climate Modeling Center FV3-based Mars Global Climate Model (c48 reference simulation, 6th simulated year), regridded to 2° × 2° (a cell is about 120 km across at the equator, larger than most dune fields): 16,032 hourly samples, one Mars year. The map draws each cell as one square, so a field that changes strongly from cell to cell, as DP often does at low latitudes, looks blocky. Air density of the lowest layer ρ = p/(R T); the height z of the lowest-level wind follows from the hourly pressure and temperature (1.5–3.2 m over all cells and hours; 1.6–3.0 m in 98 % of the hours of dune cells; the cell panel gives the range of the selected cell), and the friction velocity u* comes from the smooth-wall mixing-length profile of Pähtz & Durán (2023, eq. 2.2) under constant stress at that height (no roughness length).
  • Sand-flux fields: for every hour, the threshold and the saturated transport rate of Pähtz & Durán (2023, J. Fluid Mech. 963, A20) at the selected median grain diameter d (grain density 3000 kg/m³, g = 3.71 m/s²), averaged over the year; drift potentials, crest fluxes and dune-orientation modes follow the method of Gunn (2026). Fluxes are per Earth year (365.25 days).
  • Dune map: USGS Mars Global Digital Dune Database (MGD3; Hayward et al. 2007, 2010, 2012, 2014) plus the small dune fields of Fenton (2020, Icarus 352, 114018), merged into 3,514 dune-field polygons (Mars 2000 sphere).
  • Saturated flux divergence ${mathHtml("$\\nabla\\cdot\\vec{q}_s$")}: divergence of the resultant drift potential vector (magnitude RDP, direction RDD) on the Mars sphere (R = 3389.5 km), following Gunn (2026), Methods M6, with central differences on the 2° grid. Negative values (convergence) imply deposition.
  • Elevation and shaded relief: MGS MOLA – MEX HRSC blended DEM, 200 m, v2 (Fergason, Hare & Laura 2018, USGS Astrogeology); licence: MOLA (CC0) and HRSC (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO). The atlas's MOLA–HRSC shaded-relief basemap tiles are released under CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO (derived from HRSC, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO, and MOLA, CC0).
`;
